newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady ahead of weekend.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity in the northeastern U.S. held steady Friday versus Thursday's level ahead of a weekend that was predicted to be cool, even rainy, in much of the region, market sources said.

A five-week refueling shutdown of Niagara Mohawk Power Corp's 1,120 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point Two nuclear unit in Scriba, N.Y., triggered more daily power transactions in the New York Power Pool (NYPP) this week, traders said.
The utility was expected to begin Nine Mile Point Two's outage, the plant's fifth, on Saturday.
"Even with that coming down, prices were pretty much the same from a year ago," a NYPP trader said.
Non-firm electricity for heavy demand hours for the weekend in western NYPP was assessed at $15.00-$16.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), and eastern NYPP $17.00-$18.00.
For Monday, peak, non-firm electricity in western NYPP was quoted at $19.00-$20.00 and in eastern NYPP $23.00-$24.00.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Monday was pegged at $9.00-$13.00 in the western portion of NYPP and $14.00-$15.00 in eastern portion of NYPP.
On Thursday, western NYPP peak electricity for Friday was pegged at $19.00-$20.00, and eastern NYPP at $22.00-$23.00; Thursday's off-peak prices for Friday in NYPP was discussed near $15.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), bulking power activity for the weekend was thin, market sources said.
Weekend non-firm NEPOOL prices for heavy load hours were notationally assessed at $26.00, and light load hours $20.00.
For Monday delivery, NEPOOL non-firm electricity during peak hours was discussed in the $26.00-$28.00, with sellers offering power as high as $31.00.
Monday's non-firm, off-peak power in NEPOOL was valued near $22.00.
On Thursday, peak, non-firm electricity in NEPOOL for Friday was discussed at $28.00-$30.00.

Boston Edison Co's 670 MW Pilgrim nuclear station in Plymouth, Mass., was expected to return on line over the weekend after being shut last week due to a saltwater intrusion in a set of heat exchangers in its reactor building.
The latest forecasts showed the Northeast would receive warmer-than-normal autumn weather next week.
